importABCatlas brings data from the
[Allen Brain Cell (ABC) Atlas](https://portal.brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas)
into R. It does two things:

1. `load_data()` downloads and assembles the cell metadata of a dataset (cells
   joined with their clusters, donors, regions, ...), so you can choose cells by
   any of these properties.
2. `fetch_data()` downloads the expression matrices holding the chosen cells
   and returns their raw counts as a sparse `Seurat` object.

Everything runs in R and no Python installation is needed. Files are
downloaded once into a local folder and reused afterwards.

This vignette uses the Aging Mouse dataset as its example: it selects
striatal microglia from adult and aged mice and compares a few marker genes.

## Installation

The package depends on two Bioconductor packages, so install those first:


``` r
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("rhdf5", "HDF5Array"))

# The R-only package lives in the R_only/ folder of the repository.
remotes::install_github("me37uday/importABCatlas", subdir = "R_only", ref = "R_only")
```


``` r
library(importABCatlas)
```

## Where the data goes

ABC Atlas files are large: metadata tables take 0.5 to 1.5 GB per dataset, and
each expression matrix takes 3 to 33 GB. Choose a folder with enough space
before the first download. The folder is taken from, in order:

1. the `download_base` argument of `load_data()` and `fetch_data()`;
2. the `importABCatlas.download_base` option;
3. the `ABC_ATLAS_CACHE` environment variable;
4. a per-user cache folder (`tools::R_user_dir("importABCatlas", "cache")`).

The simplest way is to set the option once per session:


``` r
options(importABCatlas.download_base = "/data/abc_atlas")
abc_download_dir()  # shows the folder that will be used
```

The folder has the same layout as the one used by the Allen Institute's Python
package `abc_atlas_access`, so a folder already filled from Python can be
reused as is.

## Loading cell metadata

Five datasets are supported:

| `dataset` | Description |
|---|---|
| `"WHB"` | Whole human brain, 10x v3 |
| `"WMB"` | Whole mouse brain, 10x v2, v3 and Multiome |
| `"AgingMouse"` | Aging mouse brain (adult and aged), 10x v3 |
| `"HMBA"` | Human and Mammalian Brain Atlas, basal ganglia, 10x Multiome |
| `"PMDBS"` | ASAP post-mortem brain and spinal cord, 10x |

`load_data()` returns the assembled cell metadata, the gene table and, for a
few columns of interest, their distinct values:


``` r
aging <- load_data("AgingMouse")
#> AgingMouse: 1162565 cells
#> AgingMouse: 32285 genes
names(aging)
#> [1] "cell_metadata" "gene_data"     "unique_values"
dim(aging$cell_metadata)
#> [1] 1162565      66
```

There is one row per cell. The `cell_label` column identifies cells, and the
other columns describe each cell's sample, donor, region and cluster:


``` r
head(aging$cell_metadata[, c("cell_label", "donor_age_category", "donor_sex",
                             "anatomical_division_label", "subclass_name")])
#>                 cell_label donor_age_category donor_sex anatomical_division_label
#> 1 AAACCCAAGGACACTG-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#> 2 AAACCCAAGTAAACGT-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#> 3 AAACCCACATTGAGCT-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#> 4 AAACGAAAGCCGTAAG-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#> 5 AAACGAAAGCTACAAA-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#> 6 AAAGAACAGAGAGGTA-367_B04              adult         F                       STR
#>     subclass_name
#> 1 061 STR D1 Gaba
#> 2 319 Astro-TE NN
#> 3     333 Endo NN
#> 4 319 Astro-TE NN
#> 5    327 Oligo NN
#> 6     331 Peri NN
```

`unique_values` lists the distinct values of the columns most useful for
choosing cells:


``` r
lengths(aging$unique_values)
#>       anatomical_division_label                       donor_sex 
#>                               7                               2 
#>                       donor_age            cluster_name_cl_info 
#>                              30                             847 
#> neurotransmitter_combined_label 
#>                              15
aging$unique_values$anatomical_division_label
#> [1] "STR"       "Isocortex" "P"         "HPF"       "MB"        "HY"        "PAL"
```

## Choosing cells

`fetch_data()` selects cells with `filters`: a named list where each name is a
metadata column and each value lists the accepted values for that column. A
cell is kept when it matches every filter.

Before fetching expression data, check the selection on the metadata. This is
fast and does not download anything:


``` r
cells <- aging$cell_metadata
microglia_types <- grep("Microglia", unique(cells$subclass_name), value = TRUE)
microglia_types
#> [1] "334 Microglia NN"

filters <- list(anatomical_division_label = "STR",
                subclass_name = microglia_types)

selected <- cells[cells$anatomical_division_label == "STR" &
                  cells$subclass_name %in% microglia_types, ]
table(selected$donor_age_category)
#> 
#> adult  aged 
#>  4845  7695
```

`fetch_data()` downloads every expression file that contains at least one
selected cell, even when only a few of its cells are selected. You can see
which files those are with `feature_matrix_label`. The whole Aging Mouse
dataset is in a single 13.8 GB file:


``` r
unique(selected$feature_matrix_label)
#> [1] "Zeng-Aging-Mouse-10Xv3"
```

To select an exact list of cells, for instance from a previous analysis, filter
on `cell_label`:


``` r
filters <- list(cell_label = my_cell_labels)
```

## Fetching expression data

`fetch_data()` takes the metadata and gene table from `load_data()` and the
filters. It returns raw counts for all genes, or only for the gene symbols
listed in `genes`. Here it reads all genes of the selected cells:


``` r
microglia <- fetch_data(metadata = aging$cell_metadata,
                        gene_data = aging$gene_data,
                        filters = filters)
#> loading file: Zeng-Aging-Mouse-10Xv3
#> Warning: 78 gene identifiers in Zeng-Aging-Mouse-10Xv3-raw.h5ad are malformed; genes were
#> aligned by position.
microglia
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 32285 features across 12540 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: RNA (32285 features, 0 variable features)
#>  1 layer present: counts
```

The warning comes from the data, not from your selection. In the Aging Mouse
expression file, 78 gene identifiers (genes whose symbol is used by two genes)
were saved in a malformed way. The package detects this and matches those
genes by their position in the file, which is safe because the file and the
gene table list the genes in the same order.

The Seurat object holds the counts in its `RNA` assay and the cells' full
metadata:


``` r
counts <- SeuratObject::LayerData(microglia, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts")
class(counts)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "Matrix"
counts[c("P2ry12", "Cx3cr1", "Tmem119"), 1:5]
#> 3 x 5 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
#>         AAAGAACGTGCGAGTA-367_B04 AAAGAACTCGCCTTTG-367_B04 AAAGGGCTCCACTTTA-367_B04
#> P2ry12                         6                       14                       23
#> Cx3cr1                        15                       19                       24
#> Tmem119                        8                       15                       18
#>         AAAGTCCTCTCGGGAC-367_B04 AAAGTGAGTGGCTGCT-367_B04
#> P2ry12                        19                       12
#> Cx3cr1                        18                       24
#> Tmem119                        1                        6

table(microglia$donor_age_category, microglia$donor_sex)
#>        
#>            F    M
#>   adult 2339 2506
#>   aged  3151 4544
```

From here, the object can be used with any Seurat workflow. As a small example,
here is the share of microglia expressing each of a few genes, by age group:


``` r
genes <- c("P2ry12", "Tmem119", "Cx3cr1", "Apoe", "Lpl", "Cst7", "Lgals3")
expressing <- counts[genes, ] > 0
by_age <- split(colnames(microglia), microglia$donor_age_category)
round(sapply(by_age, function(cells) Matrix::rowMeans(expressing[, cells])), 2)
#>         adult aged
#> P2ry12   1.00 0.99
#> Tmem119  0.99 0.98
#> Cx3cr1   1.00 1.00
#> Apoe     0.45 0.42
#> Lpl      0.07 0.08
#> Cst7     0.01 0.05
#> Lgals3   0.01 0.02
```

The homeostatic markers `P2ry12`, `Tmem119` and `Cx3cr1` are detected in
nearly every cell of both groups. Among the markers of activated microglia,
`Cst7` is detected in a larger share of cells in aged mice. The others change
little in this raw comparison, which does not account for differences in
sequencing depth.

## Fetching only some genes

When only a few genes are needed, list them in `genes`. The download is the
same, because files are downloaded whole, but the result is much smaller:


``` r
markers <- fetch_data(metadata = aging$cell_metadata,
                      gene_data = aging$gene_data,
                      filters = filters,
                      genes = genes)
#> loading file: Zeng-Aging-Mouse-10Xv3
dim(markers)
#> [1]     7 12540
```

## Working offline

Once the files you need are downloaded, set `offline = TRUE` to use only the
local folder. The network is never contacted, and a missing file is an error
instead of a download:


``` r
aging <- load_data("AgingMouse", offline = TRUE)
microglia <- fetch_data(metadata = aging$cell_metadata,
                        gene_data = aging$gene_data,
                        filters = filters,
                        offline = TRUE)
```

## Reading other files

`abc_cache_connect()` gives direct access to every file of the current ABC
Atlas release, including tables that `load_data()` does not join. For example,
the donor table of the Aging Mouse dataset:


``` r
cache <- abc_cache_connect()
cache$manifest_name
#> [1] "releases/20260711/manifest.json"

donors <- cache$get_metadata_dataframe("Zeng-Aging-Mouse-10Xv3", "donor")
head(donors[, c("donor_label", "donor_age", "donor_sex", "donor_genotype")])
#>                    donor_label donor_age donor_sex                       donor_genotype
#> 1              C57BL/6J-592557       18M         M                                wt/wt
#> 2              C57BL/6J-592558       18M         F                                wt/wt
#> 3 Snap25-IRES2-Cre;Ai14-443008      P549         F Snap25-IRES2-Cre/wt;Ai14(RCL-tdT)/wt
#> 4 Snap25-IRES2-Cre;Ai14-450087       P56         M Snap25-IRES2-Cre/wt;Ai14(RCL-tdT)/wt
#> 5 Snap25-IRES2-Cre;Ai14-450091      P547         F                     Ai14(RCL-tdT)/wt
#> 6 Snap25-IRES2-Cre;Ai14-450095       P56         F Snap25-IRES2-Cre/wt;Ai14(RCL-tdT)/wt
```

`cache$get_file_path(directory, file_name)` returns the local path of any file,
downloading it first if needed. The directory and file names are those of the
[release manifest](https://allen-brain-cell-atlas.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/index.html).
